content.title: Nebraska vs Iowa score, highlights: Hawkeyes advance to Elite 8
content.text: Updated March 26, 2026, 10:08 p.m. ETIowa basketball only led for 2:08 of game clock against Nebraska in the 2026 Men's NCAA Tournament on Thursday, March 26, but it's moving onto the Elite Eight anyway after overcoming a 10-point deficit in the first half.The Hawkeyes and Cornhuskers were tied at 65-65 will 3:11 left in the second half, before Iowa outscored Nebraska 12-6 in the final moments, courtesy of a 3-pointer from star Bennett Stirtz and a ferocious and-one from March Madness hero Alvaro Folgueiras.Stirtz led Iowa with 20 points, but it was true freshman Tate Sage and Folgueiras off the bench who provided a huge boost with a combined 35 points. The win sets a record for the lowest-seeded Big Ten team ever to reach the Elite Eight, and it's the program's first appearance in a regional final since 1989.First-year coach Ben McCollum has done the unthinkable this season and is looking to keep it going. On the other end, Nebraska's historic run also ends, after the Cornhuskers won their first two NCAA Tournament games in program history before falling to Iowa.Here are the highlights from Iowa's win over Big Ten foe Nebraska in the Sweet 16:Nebraska vs Iowa basketball live scoreTEAMS1H2HFIowa433477Nebraska462571Nebraska vs Iowa highlights Iowa wins 77-71, advances to Elite EightIowa only leads for 2:08 of game clock but ends up defeating Nebraska 77-71 after a flurry of shots at the end of the game. The No. 9 Hawkeyes are going to the Elite Eight as the lowest-seeded Big Ten team to ever reach a Regional final. Alvaro Folgueiras converts and-1 playWow, Iowa takes advantage of Nebraska's lapse, as Alvaro Folgueiras receives the full-court inbounds pass and is fouled as he scores before converting the 3-point play. The Cornhuskers somehow only had four players on the court out of a timeout. Iowa leads 71-68 with 58 seconds leftTate Sage gives Iowa a 71-65 lead after making his fourth 3-pointer of the game, only for Braden Frager to respond with his fifth 3-point make of the game for Nebraska.Iowa regains possession with a 71-68 lead with 58 seconds left. What a game. Iowa takes first lead of gameIowa takes its first lead of the game after Bennett Stirtz nails a 3-pointer to make the score 68-65 with less than two minutes remaining. Here come the Hawkeyes. Crunch time for Nebraska-IowaNebraska and Iowa are tied at 65-65 with 3:11 left in the game. This one is going to come down to the wire, folks. Pryce Sandfort makes another 3-pointerPryce Sandfort has been unstoppable in the second half. He gives Nebraska a 65-62 lead on his fifth 3-pointer of the game, which puts him at 22 points on 7-of-9 shooting. Nebraska regains leadNebraska needs to find more shots for Pryce Sandfort, who's up to 16 points on 5-of-6 shooting, three of which have landed from 3-point range. Braden Frager is also staying hot, hitting his fourth 3-pointer of the game.Nebraska leads 58-55 with 11:30 left, and this one is looking like it'll come down to the wire. Iowa ties it at 50-50Kael Combs finds Tate Sage in transition, and Sage scores the layup to tie the game at 50-50 with 14:45 left in the second half. Iowa's defense has stepped up this half, holding Nebraska to 25% shooting and scoreless for the last 2:20 of game clock. Sam Hoiberg has four turnoversNebraska point guard Sam Hoiberg, son of coach Fred Hoiberg, just threw away his fourth turnover of the game. It has been an uncharacteristic game so far for the experienced guard who ranks fourth nationally in assist-to-turnover ratio. Tate Sage hits 3-pointer at the buzzerHave a half, Tate Sage. Sage hits another 3-pointer — his third of the first half — as the buzzer sounds to cut Iowa's deficit to 46-43 at halftime.Both teams shot lights out through 20 minutes of game action, as Iowa ends the first half at 60% shooting with seven 3-pointers compared to Nebraska 57.7% mark with seven 3s. Alvaro Folgueiras slams one homeAlvaro Folgueiras, the hero in Iowa's win over Florida, throws down a big dunk before Bennett Stirtz hits his first 3-pointer of the game on the following possession.Iowa now trails 40-35 with 3:32 left in the first half. The Hawkeyes have received a big boost off the bench from true freshman Tate Sage, who has eight points. Both offenses are rollingIowa is shooting 64.3% from the field in the early going but finds itself trailing 32-26 with 8:23 left in the first half. The difference? Nebraska, which is shooting 58.8% so far, has six 3-pointers to Iowa's four, and has also attempted four more shots already. Braden Frager is on fire for NebraskaBraden Frager is picking up where he left off after scoring the game-winning bucket against Vanderbilt in the second round. The true freshman bench wing is already 3-of-3 shooting with three 3-pointers for a game-leading nine points in the early going. Nebraska, Iowa trading 3-pointersBraden Frager nails a 3-pointer, then Iowa's Tate Sage responds with his own 3-pointer, before Frager hits another. Nebraska is already up to five 3-point makes and leads 25-17 with 11:55 left in the first half. Nebraska leads 12-2, Iowa calls timeoutPryce Sandfort hits another 3-pointer to give Nebraska a 12-2 lead over his former team with 16:54 left in the first half. Berke Buyuktuncel has three assists and two offensive rebounds already, both of which have led to Sandfort 3-pointers. Nebraska makes back-to-back 3-pointersNebraska's Jamarques Lawrence and Pryce Sandfort hit back-to-back 3-pointers early to give the Cornhuskers a 6-0 lead. The Nebraska fan base is loud, having traveled en masse again after taking over Oklahoma City in the first weekend. Starting lineups for Nebraska vs IowaHere's a look at Nebraska and Iowa's starting lineups tonight:Iowa: G Bennett Stirtz, G Kael Combs, G Tavion Banks, F Cooper Koch, F Cam ManyawuNebraska: G Sam Hoiberg, G Jamarques Lawrence, F Pryce Sandfort, F Rienk Mast, F Berke Buyuktuncel Cooper DeJean at Nebraska vs IowaFormer Iowa defensive back and current Philadelphia Eagles star Cooper DeJean is in the house to cheer on the Hawkeyes in the Sweet 16:What time is Nebraska vs Iowa Sweet 16 game today?Tip-off is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET from Houston.What channel is Nebraska vs Iowa game on? How to watch, streaming infoNebraska vs. Iowa will air on TBS and truTV and stream via Sling TV.Nebraska vs Iowa predictions, picks, oddsOdds provided by BetMGM as of 9:30 a.m., Thursday, March 26.∎ Tyler Tachman, Des Moines Register: Iowa 68, Nebraska 65The Huskers and Hawkeyes split the season series, with each of them winning on their home floors. This game, though, clearly has a lot more at stake than just a regular season Big Ten victory. Both games were very tight, with Nebraska's win earlier this month in Lincoln going to overtime with a big Iowa comeback.This game could really go either way, and regardless of the result, it would be historic. A win would earn Iowa its first trip to the Elite Eight since 1987. A victory for Nebraska would keep this historic March Madness run alive. Either way, the winner of this one will be just three wins away from a national title.Blake Toppmeyer: NebraskaPaul Myerberg: NebraskaJordan Mendoza: NebraskaJohn Brice: NebraskaMatt Glenesk: NebraskaCraig Meyer: IowaJohn Leuzzi: NebraskaAustin Curtright: IowaEhsan Kassim: NebraskaMoneyline: Nebraska (-130); Iowa (+110)Spread: Nebraska (-1.5)Over/under total: 131.5Why did Pryce Sandfort transfer from Iowa to Nebraska?Nebraska's leading scorer Pryce Sandfort transferred from Iowa to Nebraska after the Hawkeyes fired Fran McCaffery following last season.After Iowa hired Ben McCollum, every Hawkeye scholarship player except one transferred to a new home, including Pryce to Nebraska."It's like a Hollywood horror story almost,” said Pryce's older brother Payton, who starred for the Hawkeyes. “You want both teams to do so well. And they're both having dream seasons. … And now they run into each other?”“I could never not support Pryce,” he added. “I know what we’ve been through together and what we’ve dreamed about. For him to have a chance to play in the Final Four, that’s pretty special for my family. It’s just, why couldn’t it be (against) anybody else?”Is Sam Hoiberg related to Fred Hoiberg?Yes, he's his son. While Fred was known for his 3-point shooting, Sam is a nuisance on defense and earned votes for Big Ten's defensive player of the year, which went to Michigan center Aday Mara.Sam averages 9.4 ppg, 5.4 rpg and 4.3 apg.∎ Read more about the Hoibergs from USA TODAY Sports' Danielle Lerner.What happened when Iowa, Nebraska played this season?The teams split their regular season series.Iowa won 57-52 on Feb. 17Nebraska won 84-75 in OT on March 8Bennett Stirtz followed Ben McCollum from Drake to IowaThe Hawkeyes' leading scorer Bennett Stirtz (19.7 ppg) transferred from Drake to Iowa, following coach Ben McCollum. The two were key to the Bulldogs' first-round upset of Missouri in the 2025 NCAA Tournament."Yeah, the amount of trust I have in him, and that he never lies to anyone on this team, including me. He shoots it straight," Stirtz said on his relationship with McCollum. "Even when it's tough and even when it's hard. He pushes you past your limit and I think that's where the trust comes in and he cares about you a lot and wants to make you a better person. So, yeah, he just pushes everyone on this team and honestly you can see the benefit from that and even in the wins that he's all had throughout his career, he doesn't get complacent. So that's what we need to do and continue to do is even though we beat a 1 seed, we can't get complacent, we got to keep getting better every day and get ready for the game tomorrow."Why does Alvaro Folgueiras point to sky after 3-pointers?Folgueiras points up at the sky after every 3-pointer he makes in honor of his dad, who died when he was 9 years old. He pointed at the sky after hitting his eventual game-winner against Florida, although he waited for the Gators' timeout after running back on defense.Folgueiras expressed what his family means to him after the game, and mentioned his mom being a rock throughout his childhood without his dad."He left us with my mom and my brother in my house," he said. "It was kind of hard. We didn't really feel it as much because my mom always made sure that we didn't need anything, absolutely nothing. So, I cannot say that I grew up in an environment where I needed some things. No, that's not the truth."Sometimes I can say that because I feel his absence. I was just going in the court and playing to get away of my house to be with something else. But I can say that I had a happy childhood. Something that we all said, and everyone has these kinds of things on their life."It's that we are not victims. I never let things like that make me a victim. Not to me and not to my brother, not to my mom. We are like that because my mom was showing out every single day. Yeah."
